+
+Registered bots are distinguished from unverified bots that Teams identifies through its detection mechanisms. In the meeting lobby, registered bots appear in the **Waiting** section, while unverified bots detected through behavioral and infrastructure signals appear under **Suspected threats**. This distinction provides meeting organizers with additional context when reviewing participants and deciding whether to admit them. Registration identifies a bot but doesn't automatically grant it permission to join a meeting.
+

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams for Android and iOS: Update to the latest app version to maintain file access
messageCenterItems.summary: Update Microsoft Teams mobile to version 1416/1.0.0.2026151302 (Android) or 8.19.0 (iOS) by April 1, 2027, to maintain file access. Older versions will lose file functionality due to a shift to Microsoft Entra ID authentication replacing pre-authenticated URLs. Begin updates now.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We are updating how Microsoft Teams mobile authenticates access to files stored in SharePoint Online and OneDrive. To improve security, we are retiring pre-authenticated URLs and transitioning file access to Microsoft Entra ID-based authentication.

To support this change, users must run a compatible version of Teams for Android (1416/1.0.0.2026151302 or later) or iOS (8.19.0 or later). Users running older, incompatible versions may experience failures in affected file scenarios after enforcement begins on April 1, 2027. We recommend that you begin preparing now to ensure users are running compatible Teams mobile versions before enforcement begins.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in mid-March 2027 and is expected to complete by early April 2027.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users running older, incompatible versions of Microsoft Teams for Android or iOS.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams for Android
  • Microsoft Teams for iOS

What will happen

  • Beginning April 1, 2027, users running older, incompatible versions may experience failures when: 
    • Opening files shared in Teams.
    • Previewing files and thumbnails in chats and channels.
    • Downloading files from Teams.
    • Uploading and sharing files from their devices.
    • Playing videos stored in OneDrive or SharePoint within Teams.
    • Sharing slides in meetings using PowerPoint Live.
    • Sharing files with bots and agents.
  • Users running compatible Teams mobile versions will continue to access files through the affected scenarios as expected.
  • Other Teams functionality will not be affected by this change.

Action required and recommendations

To prepare for enforcement on April 1, 2027, we recommend that you begin updating users now and complete the following actions before that date:

  • Encourage users to update Microsoft Teams mobile to the latest available version.
  • Ensure Android users are running Teams version 1416/1.0.0.2026151302 or later.
  • Ensure iOS users are running Teams version 8.19.0 or later.
  • Review your mobile app management and deployment policies, where applicable, to help ensure users receive an updated Teams version.
  • Communicate the update requirement to users running older, incompatible versions.
  • Update internal help desk guidance and documentation as appropriate.

No action is required for users already running the minimum compatible version or later.

Important: Disabling pre-authenticated URLs (tempauth) through PowerShell before April 1, 2027, may disrupt file scenarios across Teams mobile, regardless of app version. We recommend avoiding this change until the scheduled enforcement date.

Learn more

  • Pre-authenticated (tempauth) URLs are retiring: move to Microsoft Entra ID tokens before April 1, 2027 - Microsoft 365 Developer Blog
  • Version update history for Teams app deployments - Office release notes | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Expanded Markdown support in the compose box
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will expand Markdown support in the compose box, allowing users to write with visible syntax, use a Markdown toolbar, preview messages, and switch between Markdown and rich text. Public preview starts mid-December 2026; general availability begins mid-January 2027. No admin action needed.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 25, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Teams is introducing an updated Markdown compose experience with expanded formatting support. Users can write and edit with Markdown syntax intact, without formatting automatically rendering as they type. A dedicated Markdown toolbar helps users insert formatting syntax, preview the rendered message before sending, and switch between Markdown and rich text.

Rollout schedule

  • Public preview: Beginning in mid-December 2026 and expected to complete by late December 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026) and expected to complete by late February 2027 (previously mid-December 2026)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams users who compose messages in chats and channels on supported platforms

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams for Windows, Mac, and web

What will happen

Users will be able to select Format in Markdown from the compose box’s Actions and apps (+) menu (Screenshot 1).

The updated experience includes:

  • Markdown authoring without live rendering: Syntax remains visible and editable while users write.
  • A dedicated Markdown toolbar: Users can insert syntax for formatting (Screenshot 2).

  • Message preview: Users can turn on Preview message to see the rendered formatting before sending (Screenshot 3).

  • Switching between compose modes: Users can select Format in rich text from the same menu to return to rich text authoring (Screenshot 4).

Teams will remember the user’s selected compose mode and apply it across chats and channels until the user switches modes.

Learn more

  • Use Markdown formatting in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support

Action required and recommendations

No admin action is required to prepare for this feature.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
